sections.heading: 1. Electric Circuit and Symbols
points: An **electric circuit** provides a **closed path** for electric current to flow (from the **+ to the − terminal** of a cell in the external circuit).
A **battery** = two or more **cells** joined together.
Standard **circuit symbols** are used to draw circuit diagrams (for cell, battery, switch, bulb, wire).
A **switch** opens/closes the circuit (open = no current; closed = current flows).

sections.heading: 2. Heating Effect of Current
points: When current flows through a wire, the wire gets **hot** — the **heating effect** of current.
The **more resistance**, the **more heat** produced; used in **electric heater, iron, geyser, toaster** (nichrome wire).
In a **bulb**, the thin **tungsten filament** glows and gives light.
An **electric fuse** is a safety device: a thin wire that **melts and breaks the circuit** if too much current flows (preventing fire).

sections.heading: 3. Magnetic Effect of Current
points: A current-carrying wire behaves like a **magnet** — the **magnetic effect** of current (discovered by **Oersted**).
A **compass needle** deflects near a current-carrying wire.
An **electromagnet** = a coil of wire wound on an **iron core**; it becomes a magnet **only when current flows** (can be switched on/off and made strong).
Electromagnets are used in **cranes, electric bells, motors, loudspeakers**.

sections.heading: 4. The Electric Bell
points: An **electric bell** works on the **magnetic effect**: when current flows, the electromagnet pulls an iron strip (armature) → hammer strikes the gong → this **breaks the circuit** → the magnet loses power → the strip springs back → circuit completes again → repeats, ringing the bell.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Circuit = closed path; battery = cells joined; switch opens/closes circuit.
Heating effect: current heats a wire (heater/iron/toaster = nichrome); bulb filament = tungsten.
Fuse = safety device (thin wire melts if excess current).
Magnetic effect (Oersted): current-carrying wire acts as a magnet; deflects a compass.
Electromagnet = coil on iron core, magnetic only when current flows; used in cranes/bells/motors.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **fuse** melts to **break** the circuit and prevent fires when current is excessive.
An **electromagnet** is a magnet **only while current flows** (unlike a permanent magnet).
The **magnetic effect** of current was discovered by **Oersted** (compass deflection).
The **electric bell** works on the **magnetic effect**, and the heater/iron on the **heating effect**.
